questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the air in a fully inflated tire

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure. You can find this information on the side of the tire.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must maintain four points of contact with the vehicle
May turn to face the road before your exit is complete
Must be facing away from the vehicle

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If your test vehicle is a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

questions.question: If convicted of a traffic violation, you must inform your employer:
questions.explanation: If you are convicted of any traffic violation, you must tell your employer within 30 days. You must also notify your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: When a vehicle is started, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes
Should turn off within a few seconds
Should stay on until you manually turn them off

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, the warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should turn off right away.

questions.question: Pressing the brake pedal causes air pressure to activate an electric switch and:

options.text: Turn on the low pressure warning light
Turn off the low pressure warning light

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, the brake lights turn on when you press the brake pedal. The air pressure moves an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: When driving with covered cargo, a cover that flaps:

options.text: Allows air to keep the cargo cool

questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind. They could tear loose and uncover the cargo or block the view of other drivers.

questions.question: Except for the straight line backing exercise, a driver may exit their vehicle to check its position during testing up to:
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during any basic vehicle control skills test exercise. This is called a "look." For the straight line backing exercise, you may only look once. For all other exercises, you may look up to two times.

questions.question: After driving under an overpass during the driving skills test, you may be asked to recall:

options.text: If there was a shoulder near the roadway

questions.explanation: If you drive under an overpass during the on-road driving skills test, your examiner may ask you what the posted clearance or height of the overpass was.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver's compartment
Maintains a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles
Lightens the load for the tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up a vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Problems with the suspension system are very dangerous.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver:

options.text: Can use any cell phone while driving
Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving
Can only use a cell phone on rural roads
Can use a cell phone at night

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicle drivers cannot use hand-held cell phones while driving.

questions.question: How do you check if a vehicle can safely carry a load?

options.text: Check the tire rating for the front tires only.
Drive the vehicle and see how it handles.

questions.explanation: It is your responsibility to make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. You must know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including the suspension system's weight capacity.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you check about the pedals?

options.text: The pedal surface should be smoothed out.
Something should be under the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that nothing is blocking or stuck under the pedals. Make sure the pedals work properly and that the pedal surfaces are grooved.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive slowly and block other traffic?
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic flow, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secure?
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement within the first 50 miles of a trip. After that, check it again every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What should you do after changing a tire?

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Look for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: How many driver licenses can you have?

options.text: A regular license from one state and a CDL from another state.
Two licenses: one for cars and one for trucks.

questions.explanation: You can have only one driver license. Having more than one license is illegal and can result in jail time and fines up to $5,000.

questions.question: How do you test the low air pressure warning light?

options.text: Engage and disengage the parking brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Disconnect and reconnect the glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: After the air system charges, test the warning light by pressing and releasing the brake pedal several times quickly. This releases air from the system, and the warning light should come on when air pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release on their own.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Using the parking brake in very wet, freezing weather can cause the brakes to freeze, which prevents the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: What happens if the exhaust system does not work properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Fumes may leak from the back of the muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: Leaks in the exhaust system are very dangerous. They can allow toxic fumes to enter the cab or sleeper area, putting drivers and passengers at risk.

questions.question: What happens if you stay in neutral too long while shifting gears?

options.text: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long while shifting can make it hard to put the vehicle into the next gear. If this happens, do not force the shift. Instead, go back to neutral, release the clutch, speed up the engine to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: What must you do if a load is too long?

options.text: Put a warning flag on the end of the load.
Transport it only between 6 p.m. and 3 a.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put a warning flag on the end of the load.
questions.explanation: You may need special equipment like warning flags or flashing lights for an over-length load. You will also need permits. Driving times may be limited to certain hours.

questions.question: What does axle weight mean?

options.text: The weight that one axle puts on the ground
How much the axle itself weighs
How much weight an axle can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight that one axle puts on the ground
questions.explanation: Axle weight is the weight that one axle or one set of axles puts on the ground.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle can fit under a bridge, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you cannot tell whether your vehicle will fit under a bridge or overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: What can happen if you overload a vehicle with cargo?

options.text: Usually it has no effect on the vehicle.
It can affect steering and braking.
It can harm the electrical system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect steering and braking.
questions.explanation: Overloading can hurt steering, braking, and speed control. Learn to spot when cargo is too heavy or not balanced properly.

questions.question: What should you do if the coolant level is low?
questions.explanation: When checking the engine, you should look at the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. The engine needs enough coolant in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: Where are the ABS warning lights on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights on the dashboard. Trailers have yellow ABS lights on the left side, either at the front or back corner.

questions.question: When is a vehicle inspection required?
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require that commercial vehicle drivers inspect their vehicles before each trip.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop a short distance later?

options.text: To check that the lug nuts are tight.
To make sure the tire is still clean.
To add air to the new tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later and recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the vehicle in first gear.

questions.explanation: When parking during the stop/start maneuver on the driving skills test, you must apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block driveways or intersections.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for tires that are not on the front of a commercial vehicle?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. All other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on a vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the vehicle's axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get a full night's sleep before your trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a full night's sleep before your trip
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before your trip. Other ways to stay alert include having someone ride with you, driving during times when you are normally awake, and avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise also helps you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: Where must hazmat placards be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: On the front, back, and both sides

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, back, and both sides
questions.explanation: Identical placards must be placed on the front, back, and both sides of any vehicle carrying hazardous materials that require placarding.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT checked during a vehicle inspection?
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, you must check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for snugness, cracks, or frays. Check that they are secure and not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: What should you do with your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting
Do not use them unless there is traffic
Check them regularly only if it is cloudy

questions.explanation: You must be aware of your surroundings at all times. Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of traffic and objects around your vehicle.

questions.question: How do states verify that a driver has only one CDL or CLP license?

options.text: By using a computerized system that connects all states
By looking through the driver's wallet

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a computerized system that connects all states
questions.explanation: All states share CDL and CLP license information in a computerized database. When you apply for a license, the state checks this database to make sure you don't already have one in another state.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of vehicle fires?
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can be caused by spilled fuel, under-inflated tires, dual tires that touch, electrical short circuits, smoking near fuel, improper fueling, loose fuel connections, and flammable or improperly loaded cargo.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The total weight of a vehicle before cargo is loaded
The total weight of cargo only
The maximum weight a vehicle is allowed to carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus all the cargo it is carrying.

questions.question: What happens to your vehicle's speed when driving uphill?

options.text: Gravity will not affect your speed
Gravity will cause your vehicle to swerve left

questions.explanation: When driving uphill, gravity pulls your vehicle backward and slows it down.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: How can you help prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Reduce air pressure in your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning risk increases when tire pressure is too low or tire tread is worn. If you hydroplane, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be judged on gear usage. Which should you avoid?

options.text: Selecting a gear that does not rev the engine
Forgetting to shift through an intersection

questions.explanation: During the driving test, select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine. Avoid grinding gears, clashing gears, and shifting during turns or intersections.

questions.question: If your drive wheels start to skid during braking, what should you do?

options.text: Steer opposite to the skid direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer opposite to the skid direction.
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, first release brake pressure so the wheels can roll again. Quickly steer where you want to go, then steer back to prevent skidding the other way.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should you use your four-way flashers?

options.text: Before you approach and cross railroad tracks
Only after you cross railroad tracks
Only if a train is approaching

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you approach and cross railroad tracks
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off after your entire vehicle has cleared the tracks.

questions.question: Which is a good rule to follow when making a turn?

options.text: Use arm signals to get attention
Turn off your turn signal before entering to avoid confusing drivers

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know what you plan to do. Keep the signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, your vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle will not roll backwards when you start moving forward from a stop. Rolling backwards could hit vehicles behind you.

questions.question: What is a problem with cargo that has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It makes a vehicle more likely to tip over
It is required during bad weather
It is required on some roads

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes a vehicle more likely to tip over
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip than cargo with a low center of gravity. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure 10 feet of cargo?
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Use at least two tie-downs no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road
The trailer disconnects from the tractor
The vehicle becomes easier to control

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires can lose grip and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
